translation.canonical_title: Men still try to lecture women about life (Mansplaining)
translation.displayed_title: Men still try to lecture women about life (Mansplaining)
translation.summary:
Mansplaining (from the English words “man” and “explaining”) is a feminist concept that emerged in the 2010s and describes a situation in which a man explains to a woman something she already knows, or even something in which she is an expert, in a potentially paternalistic or condescending tone.
The term appeared in the United States in 2008 in an article by Rebecca Solnit published on the TomDispatch website. The article, entitled Men Explain Things to Me, recounts how a man tried to explain the meaning of a book she had written herself without listening when she said that she was its author. She sees the phenomenon as a combination of overconfidence and ignorance on the part of the speaker.
